location.description: The location for which to retrieve the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' or 'New York, NY'.

function.name: search_local_docs
function.description: Searches the local knowledge base for documents that match the given natural language query and returns relevant document entries. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search query expressed in natural language, such as 'What are the symptoms of a cold?'.

limit.description: The maximum number of documents to return.

include_metadata.description: Determines whether to include metadata for the documents in the search results.

**First Studio Ghibli film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year** | Year | Winner | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **2002** | *Spirited Away* (2001) | The film received the Japan Academy Award for Picture of the Year at the 25th Japan Academy Awards ceremony held in 2002. | > *Spirited Away* was the first Ghibli feature to capture the top prize at Japan’s most prestigious film awards, a milestone that underscored the studio’s growing domestic prestige. --- ### How its box‑office success boosted Ghibli’s international popularity | Domestic performance | Global impact | |----------------------|---------------| | • Grossed **¥12 billion** (~US$100 million) in Japan – the highest‑grossing Japanese film of 2001.
• Worldwide total exceeded **US$380 million** (≈¥40 billion). | • The record‑breaking domestic receipts proved that Ghibli’s stories were commercially viable on a scale comparable to Hollywood blockbusters.
• The financial success gave the studio bargaining power when negotiating overseas distribution rights. | | • Won the **Academy Award for Best Animated Feature** (2003) and several other international accolades. | • The Oscar win amplified global media attention, turning *Spirited Away* into a “must‑see” title for Western audiences.
• Major distributors (Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures, Sony Pictures Releasing, etc.) secured wide theatrical releases in North America, Europe, and Latin America, often pairing the film with a dubbed version and a new marketing campaign. | | • Strong home‑video sales and merchandising in Japan. | • The commercial momentum translated into higher licensing fees for overseas releases, allowing Ghibli to invest in subtitling, dubbing, and localized marketing for subsequent titles. | | • Positive word‑of‑mouth among Japanese families and critics. | • The film’s success created a “halo effect”: audiences who discovered Ghibli through *Spirited Away* were eager to see other titles (*My Neighbor Totoro*, *Princess Mononoke*, *Howl’s Moving Castle*, etc.).
• This demand prompted the studio to negotiate broader theatrical windows and home‑video deals worldwide. | #### Key outcomes for Ghibli’s international profile 1. **Expanded Distribution Network** - Partnerships with major distributors opened up North American, European, and Asian markets for Ghibli’s back catalog. - Subsequent releases benefited from established theatrical chains and home‑video platforms. 2. **Brand Recognition & Cultural Export** - *Spirited Away* became a flagship example of Japanese animation excellence, positioning Ghibli as a cultural ambassador. - The film’s success encouraged governments and cultural institutions to support Ghibli’s works in festivals and educational programs. 3. **Financial Leverage for Future Projects** - The revenue generated allowed Ghibli to fund higher‑budget productions (e.g., *The Tale of the Princess Kaguya*, *When Marnie Was There*) and invest in international co‑production opportunities. 4. **Merchandising & Licensing Boom** - Global demand for Ghibli‑themed toys, apparel, and collectibles grew, creating additional revenue streams that further financed international marketing campaigns. In short, *Spirited Away*’s box‑office triumph—both domestically and globally—proved that Ghibli’s unique blend of artistry and storytelling could command blockbuster revenues. That financial proof‑point enabled the studio to secure wider releases, forge strategic partnerships, and cultivate a dedicated fanbase outside Japan, cementing Ghibli’s status as one of the world’s most beloved animation studios.
